target_customer: Originally hospital physicians and care teams; now hospitals seeking AI decision governance
problem: Clinicians texted patient information on insecure consumer apps; Medigram offered secure HIPAA-minded group messaging, and later AI decision records.
business_model: Software licensed to hospitals and physician groups (2012); current commercial model not stated
product_category: Healthcare secure messaging, later AI governance infrastructure

founders.name: Michael Chiu
education: Stanford medical student who left to start the company (Xconomy May 2012, snippet)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO. Education comes from a search snippet of Xconomy, whose page could not be opened.

competitors.name: TigerText
competitors.what: HIPAA compliant messaging with auto-deleting messages, in use at many hospitals
competitors.traction_then: Used in many hospitals per Healthcare IT Today

technical_complexity.rationale: Full stack messaging with backend, middleware and four client platforms plus security and HIPAA design for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Secure messaging was copyable; the bottom-up hospital adoption strategy was the only edge cited.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later consolidation in physician messaging (for example Medici buying DocbookMD in 2018) involved other companies; Medigram was not acquired.

market_need_then: Xconomy in May 2012 reported doctors at more than 50 hospitals and groups asked for the software, reflecting pain around texting patient data.

identity.voice_and_tone: Assertive and authority driven; Fluent is not verified (company site, 2026)

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand; similar names such as MediGraph exist.

pivots.to: AI governance and decision evidence infrastructure for healthcare
pivots.why: Not stated; current site shows different leadership and product, date unknown

outcome_analysis: Medigram launched in 2012 with a bottom-up secure messaging app against better known TigerText, and no funding beyond small seed amounts was verified. The current website describes an unrelated AI governance product under different named leaders, which suggests the original messaging business ended or was repurposed, though no source explains when or why. The cause is not public.
notes: Status Active per directory but the site presents a different business; pivot_failed is a weak inference from that, not a sourced finding. Aggregators conflict on funding ($20K, $120K, SoMa Ventures, Y Combinator, MicroVentures) so none is recorded as a round. Trademark MEDIGRAM filed 2012-02-15 and registered 2015-11-17; one aggregator lists it dead as of 2026. The 2012 Xconomy page returned 503 on fetch; its details come from search snippets.
